images.title: Where mist meets millennia
images.caption: Standing stones at Avebury in Wiltshire, England
images.desc: As morning mist drifts among the standing stones of Avebury in Wiltshire, England, the scene feels almost timeless. These ancient megaliths form part of one of the world's most remarkable prehistoric landscapes, centred on a vast Neolithic monument built around 4,500 years ago. Avebury contains the world's largest prehistoric stone circle, as well as a massive henge and stone avenues extending into the surrounding countryside. Together with nearby monuments such as Silbury Hill and West Kennet Avenue, it forms part of an extensive Neolithic complex that has fascinated generations of visitors, researchers and archaeologists.

images.title: Where history stands watch
images.caption: Kunětická hora Castle, Bohemia, Czechia
images.desc: What stories could these walls tell? Rising above eastern Bohemia in Czechia, Kunětická hora Castle has witnessed centuries of history. Dating to the late 14th century, the castle gradually evolved into an impressive fortress and noble residence. Its elevated position offered commanding views of the surrounding countryside and helped make it an important stronghold.

images.title: Nature's golden mirror
images.caption: A grove of pond cypress trees, Georgia, United States
images.desc: Reflected in calm water and glowing in the light of the setting sun, this grove of pond cypress creates a striking display of colour and symmetry. Native to the southeastern United States, the species is associated with shallow ponds, depressions and wetland habitats. This image was captured in Georgia, where these trees can be found in places such as the Okefenokee Swamp and other low-lying wetlands.

images.title: Nature's autumn soundtrack
images.caption: Autumn waterfalls near Sitovo, Plovdiv Province, Bulgaria
images.desc: In Bulgaria's Western Rhodope Mountains, autumn leaves gather beside the rushing waters of Sitovo Waterfall. Near the village of Sitovo, southwest of Plovdiv, the falls tumble beneath an old stone bridge whose arch frames the cascades like a storybook scene. Moss-covered stones and pine trees add shades of green to the autumn landscape, while fallen leaves gather along the water's edge or drift through its pools. The falls become especially lively after rain and during spring snowmelt, when the surrounding woodland echoes with the sound of rushing water.

images.copyright: Grand Canal in Venice, Italy (© Juan Romero/Cavan Images)
images.title: The road that runs on water
images.caption: Grand Canal in Venice, Italy
images.desc: What if a city's busiest street had no road? In Venice, Italy, traffic flows along the Grand Canal, a 3.9-kilometre waterway that winds through the city in a giant reverse S-shape. Known to locals as the Canalazzo, it is Venice's main water-traffic corridor, carrying vaporetti, water taxis, gondolas, police boats and other vessels. The canal follows the course of an ancient river that once flowed into the Venetian Lagoon.

images.title: Bookishly extravagant
images.caption: Royal Portuguese Cabinet of Reading, Rio de Janeiro, Brazil
images.desc: Today we're inside the Royal Portuguese Cabinet of Reading in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, where the humble act of opening a book took on grand architectural ambitions. Founded in 1837 by 43 Portuguese immigrants, just 15 years after Brazil's independence, the institution eventually moved into the building seen here, completed half a century later in a lavish Neo-Manueline style. Shelves soar over 20 metres around a vast reading room, crowned by a monumental stained-glass skylight that makes daylight part of the design.

images.title: Still waters, vivid colours
images.caption: Autumn in Naejangsan National Park, South Korea
images.desc: Few places in South Korea capture the magic of autumn quite like Naejangsan National Park, where mountainsides glow in brilliant shades of scarlet, orange, yellow and gold. Located in the country's southwest, the park is particularly famous for its vivid maple colours, making it one of Korea's premier destinations for autumn scenery. Its name, meaning 'many secrets in the mountains,' reflects the varied landscapes found throughout the region.
